user.title: MySQL connection
user.description: Enter the details of the MySQL or MariaDB server. The connection is tested before it is saved.

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the database server.
data_description.port: Port the server listens on. The default is 3306.
data_description.username: User the queries run as. Read only rights are enough.
data_description.database: Database used for queries that do not name one themselves.
data_description.use_tls: Encrypts the traffic to the database. The server must have TLS configured; the connection fails if it does not. The server certificate is not verified, so this protects against reading along on the network, not against a server impersonating yours. Off by default so existing setups keep working.

reconfigure.title: MySQL connection
reconfigure.description: Change where and how the connection is made. The new settings are tried before they are saved. The sensors are changed under Configure.

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the database server.
data_description.port: Port the server listens on. The default is 3306.
data_description.username: User the queries run as. Read only rights are enough.
data_description.password: Leave empty to keep the current password.
data_description.database: Database used for queries that do not name one themselves.
data_description.use_tls: Encrypts the traffic to the database. The server must have TLS configured; the connection fails if it does not. The server certificate is not verified, so this protects against reading along on the network, not against a server impersonating yours.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The database refused the username or password of {connection}. Enter the credentials to use from now on.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the server. Check the host, the port and your firewall. Details: {error}
error.invalid_auth: The server refused the username or password.
error.unknown_database: The database does not exist, or this user has no access to it.
error.connection_refused: The server refused the connection, and waiting does not fix this. The reason says what to change, for instance the host the account may connect from, a locked account or an expired password. Details: {error}
error.tls_unavailable: The server accepted the connection but did not encrypt it. Configure TLS on the database, or turn the encryption option off.

abort.already_configured: This database is already set up.

init.title: MySQL sensors
init.description: Add, edit or remove the sensors of this connection. The connection itself is changed with Reconfigure, in the menu of the connection.

add_sensor.title: Add a sensor
add_sensor.description: By default the state of the sensor is the number of rows the query returns. Fill in a column or a template to report a value from the result set instead.

data_description.query: The SQL query to run, for example SELECT * FROM emp. Only a single reading statement is allowed; it is tested against the database before it is saved.
data_description.value_column: Column of the selected row to use as the state.
data_description.value_template: Template that returns the state. Takes precedence over the value column. The variables row, rows and row_count are available.
data_description.state_class: Needed for long term statistics. The value has to be numeric.
data_description.max_json_rows: 0 keeps the whole result set. Set a limit when the query can return many rows: the whole set is held in the state of the sensor.

edit_sensor.title: Edit {name}
edit_sensor.description: By default the state of the sensor is the number of rows the query returns. Fill in a column or a template to report a value from the result set instead.

data_description.value_column: Column of the selected row to use as the state.
data_description.value_template: Template that returns the state. Takes precedence over the value column. The variables row, rows and row_count are available.
data_description.state_class: Needed for long term statistics. The value has to be numeric.
data_description.max_json_rows: 0 keeps the whole result set. Set a limit when the query can return many rows: the whole set is held in the state of the sensor.

remove_sensor.title: Remove sensors
remove_sensor.description: The selected sensors and their history are removed.

error.name_exists: A sensor with this name already exists.
error.query_multiple_statements: Only one statement is allowed in a query.
error.query_not_read_only: Only SELECT-style statements are allowed; ha_mysql only reads the database.
error.query_no_results: The query works but returned no rows. Check it, or submit it again to save it anyway.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the database. Check the host, the port and your firewall. Details: {error}

invalid_auth.message: The database refused the username or password of "{connection}". Enter new credentials to continue.

unknown_database.message: The database of "{connection}" does not exist, or its user has no access to it. A new password does not fix this: check the database name and the privileges of the user, and correct them with Reconfigure.

connection_refused.message: The database server refused the connection of "{connection}": {error}. Waiting does not fix this. The reason says what to change, for instance the host the account may connect from, a locked account or an expired password.

cannot_connect.message: Could not connect to "{connection}": {error}. Home Assistant tries again by itself.

tls_unavailable.message: "{connection}" is set to use TLS, but the server accepted the connection without encrypting it. Configure TLS on the database, or turn the encryption option off with Reconfigure.

query_not_read_only.message: Only SELECT-style statements are allowed; ha_mysql only reads the database.

query_multiple_statements.message: Only one statement is allowed in a query.

values_without_query.message: values needs a new query in the same call; without one there is no query to bind the values to.

deprecated_yaml.title: The HA MySQL configuration in configuration.yaml is deprecated
deprecated_yaml.description:
Configuring HA MySQL in configuration.yaml is deprecated and stops working in ha_mysql 2.0.0. The connection and its sensors are already stored in Home Assistant, so nothing is lost when the YAML goes.

Remove both the `ha_mysql:` section and the sensors with `platform: ha_mysql` from configuration.yaml, and restart Home Assistant. From then on, manage the sensors through Configure and the connection through Reconfigure.

set_query.name: Set query
set_query.description: Replaces the query of a sensor and refreshes it immediately. Leave the query empty to restore the query from the configuration; only SELECT-style statements are allowed.

query.name: Query
query.description: The SQL query to execute from now on. Write a %s placeholder for each value in the values field, in the same order; a literal percent sign has to be doubled to %%.

values.name: Values
values.description: Optional list of values for the %s placeholders in the query, in the order the placeholders appear. Bound separately from the query text, so the database escapes them instead of them being part of the statement. Requires a new query in the same call.

persist.name: Persist
persist.description: Save this query (and its values) so a restart re-runs it through the sensor's normal polling instead of falling back to the sensor's configured query. Resetting to the configured query always drops a previously persisted one, whether or not this is set.

select_record.name: Select record
select_record.description: Selects the row of the result set that is exposed through the valueof_ attributes. The first row is number 0.

rownumber.name: Row number
rownumber.description: Zero based index of the row to select.
